clue.text: Hit second vehicle

parts.note: a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A driver reports a collision with another car.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, meaning to have hit something.

clue.text: What starts Popeye in breaking chains?

definitions.text: What starts Popeye in breaking chains?

indicators.note: breaking the letters shatters their order, so they are rearranged
starts points to the opening letter of the name that follows

explanation.surface: The cartoon sailor gets his strength to snap chains from something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges P plus CHAINS. The whole clue is the definition: the vegetable is what powers Popeye up.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor gains superhuman strength by eating a can of the leafy green vegetable.

clue.text: Right to give out terms of reference

parts.note: to emit is to give out

explanation.surface: A committee's right to publish its brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of authority or task assigned to a person or body.

clue.text: Broken bolt on cellar is open for management

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: With the bolt broken, the cellar is open for anyone to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be managed is said to be manageable, able to be directed.

clue.text: One is grabbed by deranged girl

indicators.note: being grabbed by something means being held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: deranged means mad
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone is seized by a girl who has lost her mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid is an old-fashioned word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: A moggy about to steal tumbler

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: moggy is British slang for a cat
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A cat is about to pinch a drinking glass.
explanation.walkthrough: A moggy is everyday British slang for a cat, usually a mongrel one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is a gymnast who does somersaults, as an acrobat does.

clue.text: Excellent American man who is well dressed

definitions.meaning: ... is American slang for excellent, as in fine and ...
a man devoted to smart clothes

explanation.surface: A fine American gentleman in sharp clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandy is US slang for first-rate, and a fop who cares greatly about his appearance.

clue.text: Son is into black example of humour

indicators.note: is into means goes inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: jet is a deep black

explanation.surface: A boy is a fan of dark comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a joke, an instance of something said to amuse.

clue.text: Mentally affecting Hitchcock film running

parts.note: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller
a machine that is running is active

explanation.surface: A disturbing Hitchcock film is being shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoactive drugs alter the mind, changing mood or perception.

clue.text: Very big chaps breaking into dilapidated semi

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece sits within the other
a dilapidated house is falling apart, so its letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: chaps means men

explanation.surface: Some men break into a run-down semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilapidated' gives IMSE and 'breaking into' sets the chaps in its middle. A semi is a British semi-detached house, one of a joined pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense is a synonym for enormous or huge.

clue.text: Father has new attractive female

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father has a new girlfriend who is good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman, after the singing temptresses of Greek myth.

clue.text: Run in a northern strategy from southern Region?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the others

parts.note: a tactic is a strategy or plan
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An expedition's northern strategy for running a southern region is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside TACTIC, after A and N. The question mark flags that the definition is cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Antarctic describes things belonging to the polar area at the bottom of the globe.

clue.text: Little child wanting a black horse

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a baby is a little child
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A toddler wants a black pony.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat and black mane.

clue.text: Destroying Hydra around lake only with great difficulty

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters are wrapped about one more letter
destroying the word breaks its letters into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Killing the many-headed Hydra by a lake was a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroying' makes HARDY, and 'around' wraps it about the lake's letter, near its end. The mythical beast is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly can mean barely, achieved with severe effort.

clue.text: Shabby to cancel whiskey in Royal Navy

indicators.note: in says the pieces sit within another

parts.note: to undo is to cancel or reverse
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sailor sneers at the order to stop serving whiskey in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-down describes a place neglected and in poor repair, looking tatty.

clue.text: Weaver finding support

definitions.meaning: Nick ... is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
the ... of something is its base, the part that supports it

explanation.surface: A craftsperson at the loom finds help.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom is the Shakespearean weaver, and also the base or foundation of a structure.

clue.text: Mother and Yankee have spoken of local dignitary

parts.note: ma is mother
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Mum and an American have had a word with the town's leading figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral is the adjective relating to a mayor, a town's civic head.

clue.text: Author lifting a piece of Spenser

indicators.note: lifting means stealing, so a piece is taken straight out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A writer plagiarises a passage from the poet Spenser.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside SPENSER. Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen is a dated word for a writer, as in a hired pen.

clue.text: Puzzle show-off

explanation.surface: A conundrum about a vain person.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a tricky problem, and also a person who strikes attitudes for attention.

clue.text: Actuary upset about company reversing very firm rule

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters surround another piece
upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged
reversing says the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: An insurance statistician is upset about a firm going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives AUTRACY; 'about' wraps it round the firm's abbreviation, turned by 'reversing'. 'firm' looks like an adjective with 'rule' but is the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocracy is government by a single ruler holding absolute power.

clue.text: Time to do something in diplomacy

parts.note: to act is to do something

explanation.surface: It is time to take action through diplomatic means.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitivity in dealing with others, the core skill of a diplomat.

clue.text: Fruit beer — keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
PP, pianissimo, is the musical notation for very quiet

explanation.surface: A fruit beer is kept very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: Earth holds power to go bad

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: earth means soil

explanation.surface: Soil containing a power source starts to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that spoils decays and becomes inedible.

clue.text: Trimmer sailing vessel that goes quickly

definitions.meaning: a tool for trimming, such as hair or nails
a fast sailing ship of the 19th century

explanation.surface: A neater sailing ship moves at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clippers cut hair or hedges, and clipper ships were built for speed in the tea trade.

clue.text: Hindu queen managed India

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A queen ruled over India.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is the wife of a rajah or an Indian princess ruling in her own right.

clue.text: Something for breakfast? It's nice, really — in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone praises a breakfast dish as partly rather nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'It's' in the definition; it is a link word, since 'It's' cannot stand for the answer in a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal such as cornflakes is a typical morning meal.
